texts.error.bad_machine: '%1' is not a machine this core has.
texts.error.chd_before_start: A seek went before the start of a track of the CHD image.
texts.error.chd_gdrom: "%1" is a CHD image of a GD-ROM, which is not a CD.
texts.error.chd_no_file: The CHD image has no file "%1".
texts.error.chd_no_tracks: "%1" is a CHD image with no CD tracks in it.
texts.error.chd_not_cd: "%1" is a CHD image, but not of a CD.
texts.error.chd_not_opened: "%1" could not be opened as a CHD image: %2
texts.error.chd_past_end: A read went past the end of a track of the CHD image.
texts.error.chd_read_only: A CHD image is not written to.
texts.error.chd_sector: The CHD image could not be read at sector %1: %2
texts.error.chd_short: "%1": the CHD image is shorter than its tracks.
texts.error.chd_track_kind: "%1": track %2 of the CHD image is of a kind (%3) this core does not read.
texts.error.chd_track_nonsense: "%1": a track record of the CHD image makes no sense.
texts.error.chd_track_unreadable: "%1": a track record of the CHD image is not readable.
texts.error.no_disc: No disc is in the project.
texts.error.no_file: No game file is in the project.
texts.error.no_stv_bios: The ST-V's BIOS set (stvbios.zip) was not given: %1
texts.error.panel_stale: The control table (panel.inc) is not this Mednafen's: %1 of %2.
texts.error.stv_bios_missing: The BIOS set (stvbios.zip) does not hold the BIOS of a %1 ST-V, which MAME names %2. The game's region, or the Region setting, asks for it.
texts.error.stv_split: The ROM set has to hold every file of the game, under the names MAME gives them. A set that leaves out the files its parent set has (a "split" clone) is not read.
texts.error.stv_unknown: No file of this ROM set is the start of an ST-V game that Mednafen knows. The files have to carry the names MAME gives them (for example mpr17945.1).
texts.firmware.game_cart.about: This game was sold with a ROM cartridge and reads part of itself from it. The file is the cartridge's ROM, under the name MAME gives it. It is needed while the Cartridge setting is 'auto'.
texts.firmware.lynxboot_img.about: The Lynx's boot ROM (512 bytes). The console starts from it and it checks the cartridge. It is Atari's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.pcfx_rom.about: The PC-FX's BIOS (1 MB). The console starts from it. It is usually named pcfx.rom; versions 1.00 and 1.01 both work. It is NEC's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.satar4mp_bin.about: The ROM of the Action Replay 4M Plus cartridge. It is needed when the Cartridge setting is 'ar4mp'. You have to supply it.
texts.firmware.saturn_jp.about: The BIOS of a Japanese Saturn (512 KB). The console starts from it. Version 1.01 is usually named sega_101.bin; versions 1.00 and 1.003 work as well. It is Sega's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.saturn_na_eu.about: The BIOS of a North American or European Saturn (512 KB). The console starts from it. It is usually named mpr-17933.bin. It is Sega's and you have to supply it.
texts.firmware.stvbios_zip.about: The BIOS of the ST-V board, as the set of them MAME uses: stvbios.zip, a zip of the BIOS of every region (512 KB each). The core takes out the one for the game's region, by its contents and not by its name, so a set from any version of MAME works. It is Sega's and you have to supply it.
texts.setting.initialtime.about: What the machine's clock shows when it is switched on, in seconds since 1970 (Unix time). The Saturn's clock and the ST-V's are set from it. This is a setting, and not your computer's clock, so that a movie plays back the same on any day.
texts.setting.lynx_lowpass.about: Passes the sound through a filter like the console's small speaker. It changes the sound, so a movie's recording needs the same value.
texts.setting.lynx_rotateinput: Turn The Pad With The Screen
texts.setting.lynx_rotateinput.about: Some games are played with the console held upright. This turns the direction pad with the picture, so Up is still up. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which console this project is for. Everything else depends on it, so changing it restarts the core.
texts.setting.pcfx_adpcm_emulate_buggy_codec.a: Plays compressed sound the way the faulty tool some games were made with expected it. Mednafen says it is not accurate, only better for those games. It changes the sound, so a movie's recording needs the same value.
texts.setting.pcfx_adpcm_suppress_channel_rese: Removes the clicks heard when a game resets a sound channel. It changes the sound, so a movie's recording needs the same value.
texts.setting.pcfx_cdspeed.about: How many times faster than the real drive the disc is read. 2 is the console's own speed. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pcfx_cpu_emulation.about: How closely the processor's timing is followed. 'accurate' counts every step, 'fast' does not, and 'auto' uses 'accurate' for the games known to need it. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pcfx_high_dotclock_width.about: How many pixels wide the picture is handed out in the console's highest horizontal resolution: 341 is the real number of pixels, 256 loses detail, 1024 keeps every mode the same width. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.pcfx_input_port1_multitap.about: Plugs a multitap into the console's first controller socket. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pcfx_input_port2_multitap.about: Plugs a multitap into the console's second controller socket. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pcfx_nospritelimit.about: Draws more than the console's 16 sprites on a line. It removes flicker and can show things a game meant to hide. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.pcfx_rainbow_chromaip.about: Smooths the colour of the console's video playback between pixels. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.pcfx_slend.about: The last line of the picture that is shown. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.pcfx_slstart.about: The first line of the picture that is shown. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.port.pcfx.about: What is plugged into port %1. Only port 1 starts with a pad; give the other players theirs here. Ports 1 and 2 are the console's own. Ports 3, 4 and 5 are the extra ones of a multitap in the first socket, and ports 6, 7 and 8 those of one in the second. 'none' leaves the port empty. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.port.saturn.about: What is plugged into port %1. Only port 1 starts with a pad; give the other players theirs here. Ports 1 and 2 are the console's own when no multitap is plugged in. With a multitap in the first socket, ports 1 to 6 are on it and the next port is the second socket. 'none' leaves the port empty. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_cart.about: What is in the cartridge slot. 'auto' picks what the game is known to need and the backup memory cartridge otherwise. 'backup' is a memory cartridge for saves, 'extram1' and 'extram4' are the 1 MB and 4 MB RAM cartridges some games require, 'cs1ram16' is a 16 MB RAM cartridge for homebrew, and 'ar4mp' is the Action Replay 4M Plus, which needs its own ROM file. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_cart_auto_default: Cartridge When The Game Needs None
texts.setting.ss_cart_auto_default.about: The cartridge that 'auto' plugs in for a game that is not known to need one. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_correct_aspect.about: Shows the picture in the shape it had on a television. Turn it off to show the pixels as squares. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.ss_h_blend.about: Blurs each line a little from left to right, as a television did. Some games rely on it to mix colours. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.ss_h_overscan.about: Shows the strips at the left and right edges of the picture that a television hid. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.ss_input_sport1_multitap.about: Plugs a six-player multitap into the console's first controller socket. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_input_sport2_multitap.about: Plugs a six-player multitap into the console's second controller socket. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_region_autodetect.about: Takes the console's region from the game's disc. Turn it off to use the region set below, for a disc that names several regions or the wrong one. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_region_default.about: The console's region when it is not taken from the game: jp is Japan, na North America, eu Europe, kr Korea, tw Taiwan, as Asia, br Brazil, la Latin America. Japan and Taiwan use the Japanese BIOS file and the others the North American and European one. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_slend.about: The last line of the picture that is shown on an NTSC console. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.ss_slendp.about: The last line of the picture that is shown on a PAL console. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.ss_slstart.about: The first line of the picture that is shown on an NTSC console. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.ss_slstartp.about: The first line of the picture that is shown on a PAL console. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.ss_smpc_autortc.about: Sets the console's clock and language when the machine starts, so the BIOS does not stop to ask for them. The time is the Starting Clock setting. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.ss_smpc_autortc_lang.about: The language the console is set to when the clock is set at start. Games read it to choose their own language. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.stv_region.about: The region of the board, which decides the BIOS it starts from and, in many games, the language. 'game' is the region Mednafen's list gives the game. 'jp' is Japan, 'na' North America and 'eu' Europe; not every game runs in every region. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.vb_3dmode: How The Two Eyes Are Shown
texts.setting.vb_3dmode.about: The console shows a picture to each eye. 'anaglyph' puts both on one picture in two colours for coloured glasses, 'sidebyside' puts them next to each other, 'cscope' is the layout of a CyberScope viewer, 'vli' and 'hli' weave them line by line, and 'left' and 'right' show one eye only. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.vb_3dreverse.about: Gives the left eye's picture to the right eye and the right eye's to the left. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.vb_anaglyph_preset.about: The two colours of the 'anaglyph' picture, named after the glasses they suit. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.vb_cpu_emulation.about: How closely the processor's timing is followed. 'accurate' counts every step and a few games need it. 'fast' is Mednafen's default. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.vb_disable_parallax.about: Draws both eyes' pictures the same, with no depth. It changes the picture only.
texts.setting.vb_input_instant_read_hack.about: Gives the game the pad's buttons at the moment it asks for them and not after the console's real delay of a frame. It is Mednafen's default. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.vb_instant_display_hack.about: Shows a frame as soon as it is drawn and not when the console's displays would light it. It changes which frame a picture belongs to, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.vb_sidebyside_separation.about: The number of empty pixels between the two pictures of the 'sidebyside' layout. It changes the picture only.
texts.slot.cart.help: The game's cartridge: a .vb or .vboy file for the Virtual Boy, a .lnx file for the Lynx.
texts.slot.disc.help: The game's CD image: a .cue file with the track files it names beside it, or a .chd file. For a game on several discs, list them all in order. The first is in the drive when the console starts.
texts.slot.romset.help: The game's ROM set: a .zip of the ROM files of the game's chips, under the names MAME gives them (for example vfremix.zip). The game is known by what is inside the zip, not by the zip's own name. The zip has to hold every file of the game; a set that leaves out the files its parent set has is not read. The board's BIOS is not part of it: it is asked for on the Firmware page (stvbios.zip).
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the machine's save memory holds at the start, for a project that begins from a saved game. These are the files that Emulator > Export Save Data... writes. Saturn: a .bkr file is the console's own backup memory and a .bcr file the backup memory cartridge's. PC-FX: a .sav file is the console's own backup memory and a .fxb file the memory pack's. Virtual Boy: a .sav file is the cartridge's save memory. ST-V: a .bkr file is the board's backup memory, where a game keeps its scores and its operator settings, and a .seep file the board's own settings memory. Files of the same kinds from Mednafen work as they are. The file is never changed. Leave this empty to start with empty memory.
texts.slot.savedata.name_help: a save file is identified by its extension: .bkr and .bcr for the Saturn, .sav and .fxb for the PC-FX, .sav for the Virtual Boy, .bkr and .seep for the ST-V.
texts.suggest.japan: This disc is for a Japanese or Taiwanese console, which starts with the Japanese BIOS.
texts.suggest.needs_cart: The game needs its ROM cartridge (%1).
texts.suggest.no_region: This disc does not say which region it is for, so the Region setting decides which BIOS the console starts with.
texts.suggest.not_japan: This disc is for a console outside Japan and Taiwan, which starts with the North American and European BIOS.
